2609.02292.title: SCX Router: Streaming Zero-Shot Model Selection with a Decoder-KV Classifier and a Real-World Task Ontology
2609.02292.paper_summary: The rapid proliferation of large language models (LLMs) and the growing diversity of their applications presents a unique optimization opportunity: selecting the right model for the task, while optimizing for speed, cost, and quality at a per-task level. However, inference endpoints can vary widely in quality, price, latency, context support, tool use, domain expertise, and reasoning behavior. This heterogeneity makes manual heuristics difficult to maintain and unlikely to achieve consistently favorable speed--cost--quality trade-offs on their own. We introduce \router{}, a lightweight GLiClass-based router that assigns a suitability score to each inference-time model label without autoregressive generation. The released 0.6B-parameter checkpoint combines a Qwen3 decoder with a shallow bidirectional scorer. Its decoder-KV execution path preserves a text-only key--value cache across a session, encodes only new dialogue turns, and evaluates transient candidate-label tokens without adding them to the persistent cache. The same checkpoint also predicts task type, difficulty, reasoning mode, and expected output length, and supports custom zero-shot labels. For task generation, we construct a task ontology with 23 families, 115 task types, 345 routable subtypes, 1,173 synthetic examples, and an orthogonal axis of 30 domains. Using this structure, we generate 150,000 verifier-scored tasks and 15,000 open-ended tasks. We then train the Qwen3 decoder on these tasks, while explicitly separating learned request prediction from per-task policies for attributes such as eligibility, cost, cache reuse, safety, and sovereignty. Across six LiveBench subsets, the router outperforms the mean candidate; on the selected 1,000-task subset, it achieves an aggregate top-1 score of 0.707 versus 0.696 for the strongest fixed model, with benchmark-dependent gains.
2609.02292.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）的快速擴散及其應用的日益多樣化帶來了一個獨特的優化機會：為任務選擇合適的模型，同時在每個任務層面上優化速度、成本和質量。然而，推理端點在質量、價格、延遲、上下文支持、工具使用、領域專業知識和推理行為等方面可能差異很大。這種異質性使得手動啟發式方法難以維持，並且不太可能單獨實現持續有利的速度-成本-質量權衡。我們介紹了\router{}，一個輕量級的基於GLiClass的路由器，為每個推理時模型標籤分配適用性分數，而不進行自回歸生成。釋出的0.6B參數檢查點結合了Qwen3解碼器和一個淺層雙向評分器。其解碼器-KV執行路徑在會話中保留了一個僅限文本的鍵-值緩存，只編碼新的對話輪次，並在不將其添加到持久緩存中的情況下評估瞬態候選標籤令牌。相同的檢查點還預測任務類型、難度、推理模式和預期輸出長度，並支持自定義零樣本標籤。為了生成任務，我們構建了一個包含23個家族、115個任務類型、345個可路由子類型、1,173個合成示例和30個領域的正交軸的任務本體。利用這一結構，我們生成了150,000個驗證者評分的任務和15,000個開放式任務。然後，我們在這些任務上訓練Qwen3解碼器，同時明確區分學習的請求預測與每個任務的屬性政策，如資格、成本、緩存重用、安全性和主權。在六個LiveBench子集上，該路由器的表現超過了平均候選者；在選定的1,000任務子集上，其總體頂級分數達到0.707，而最強的固定模型為0.696，並且獲得了基準依賴的增益。
